reading: The proposal changes one thing: the open question about the Book 20 hands-to-draw conversion. The baseline asked whether the conversion is a lasting settlement or a stage the finale must revisit (E5). The proposal asks whether it reaches the shares the Mill Compact purchased or leaves them outside it, and marks that as not decided (E9). The instruction asks for exactly this rewording and no answer (E1). The Compact-settlement and lowland-obligation questions keep their wording (E14, E18).

concerns.title: Is the Book 20 conversion lasting or a stage to revisit
concerns.earlier: Asks whether the conversion is a lasting settlement or a stage the finale must revisit.
concerns.proposed: Asks only whether the conversion reaches Compact-purchased shares; lasting-versus-stage is not stated.
concerns.reading: The proposed wording no longer mentions the lasting-or-stage framing. Interpretation: that concern may need separate consideration. The record does not show whether dropping it was meant, and Book 24 still treats it as the question it makes concrete.
counterevidence: E9 marks the reach question as not decided, so the conversion's standing stays open.
E1 asks to change only wording and does not say to drop the earlier framing.
concerns.competing_reading: Reach may be a precondition for judging lasting or stage, so the earlier concern stays implicit rather than displaced.

concerns.title: Conversion reach over Compact-purchased shares
concerns.proposed: Whether the conversion applies to the Mill Compact's purchased shares or those shares stay outside it.
concerns.reading: This is a new question in the Architecture's question list. The discovery origin says the Architecture does not now state whether purchased draw is covered (E3). The selected alternative explores one answer, which goes beyond the record (E2). Interpretation: either answer changes what lowland parties owe Ammen.
counterevidence: The proposal records no answer; E9 says not decided.

concerns.title: Compact settlement through grain-labour
concerns.reading: The wording is unchanged (E14) and Book 24 records Oona's offer as neither accepted nor refused (E13). Interpretation: its meaning may shift, since E2 reads grain-labour as the Compact's in-kind answer if the conversion reaches its shares. That reading comes from the selected alternative and is not recorded.
counterevidence: E13 is recorded by identity and does not show Book 24 depends on conversion reach.

concerns.title: What lowland towns and Ammen owe each other
concerns.reading: The broad lowland-obligation question is unchanged (E18). The discovery origin links it to the conversion-reach question (E3), so its context may widen, but its wording stays as before.

prospective.text: Book 24 holds a decision on the conversion question, now reworded, and another on Compact grain-labour that is unchanged. This is a relationship by identity, not a shown contradiction. Book 25 was listed by title only, so nothing is known about its decisions.

Speculation: if the author later decides the conversion reaches purchased shares, the Compact would owe an unreturned-hands balance, and grain-labour could be the in-kind settlement. If it does not, the conversion binds only households, which sharpens the cost of counting (E3).

alternatives.title: One wording holding both conversion concerns
alternatives.summary: Speculative option. Word the question so it asks whether the conversion is lasting or a stage and whether it reaches Compact-purchased shares. It keeps the conversion question and keeps the Compact-settlement question beside it.
alternatives.gains: Keeps the earlier lasting-or-stage framing and adds reach, while still changing only one question's wording.
alternatives.costs: A compound question that can be harder to answer and to track in later Books.
alternatives.next_investigation: Check how Book 24's conversion decision (E8) reads against a compound wording.

alternatives.title: Reach and permanence as separate questions
alternatives.summary: Speculative option. Keep the baseline conversion question as it was and add a distinct reach question, described here and not given an identity. It keeps q-conversion-settlement and q-compact-settlement.
alternatives.gains: Nothing in the baseline framing is lost, and each question can be answered on its own.
alternatives.costs: Goes beyond the instruction to change only one question's wording and lengthens the question list.
alternatives.next_investigation: Ask the author whether adding a question is acceptable under E1.

alternatives.title: Keep baseline wording and carry reach under Compact settlement
alternatives.summary: Speculative option. Leave the conversion question unchanged and treat reach as part of the Compact-settlement and lowland-obligation questions it already touches.
alternatives.gains: No change to Book 24's recorded conversion decision (E8).
alternatives.costs: Reach stays implicit and may go unexamined, which E3 says leaves a gap.
alternatives.next_investigation: Check whether E13 and E15 already imply an answer on reach.

not_established: Whether dropping the lasting-or-stage framing was intended; E1 does not say.
Whether Book 25 bears on these questions; it was listed by title only (E25).
Whether Book 24's decisions depend on conversion reach; only identity is recorded.
The Architecture's other elements were not changed by the proposal and are not evaluated here.
